gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the two-bay NAS options cost on their makers' own US stores today: UGREEN DH2300 $239.99, TerraMaster F2-425 $269.99 and UGREEN DXP2800 $389.99, all read 2026-11-17. That makes the DH2300 the cheapest maker-priced two-bay box for SMB direct play to Infuse.
standout_why: I compared the two cited Firecore pages (support article 'Streaming From a Mac, PC, or NAS' and firecore.com/infuse). Between them they list the protocols (SMB, NFS, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, FTPES, UPnP, DLNA, WebDAV), the Infuse Pro prices and tvOS 18.5+. Neither names any NAS brand, model or price. ChatGPT's answer did show card prices: Synology DS124 at $160.99 (Newegg) and UGREEN DH2300 at $239.99 (Micro Center). So my DH2300 price only confirms what the shopper already saw. The new part is limited to the maker-store prices for the F2-425 and DXP2800 and a dated QNAP TS-133 price. I could not open any page that prices the DS124, which is ChatGPT's actual pick.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN DH2300 as the cheapest two-bay pick at $239.99 on UGREEN's own store, the same as ChatGPT's Micro Center card. The next maker-priced two-bay, the TerraMaster F2-425 at $269.99, costs $30 more. Our DXP2800 at $389.99 costs $150 more, and the extra spend buys x86/Docker transcoding headroom that Infuse direct play does not need. Among one-bay boxes, the QNAP TS-133 was $194.91 at AVADirect. I could not verify the DS124 price, so on sourced figures alone I can't confirm or overturn ChatGPT's 'cheapest dedicated NAS' claim.

findings.label: What Firecore says a NAS needs for Infuse
findings.value: Infuse connects over SMB, NFS, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, FTPES, UPnP, DLNA and WebDAV. No hardware or network-speed requirement and no NAS model is named. It notes that SMB3 encryption 'can lead to lower performance'.
